title: Student notes: counting gannet nests
bodyMd:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes.

- Ecologists monitoring the gannet colony on Skellan Rock, a small island in the North Atlantic, have used two methods to count nests.
- In a boat count, two observers circle the island and count nests on the cliffs through binoculars.
- A boat count takes about six hours and costs roughly 1,500 euros.
- In a drone count, a drone photographs the cliffs and software counts the nests in the images.
- A drone count needs only about ninety minutes of flying but costs roughly 4,000 euros, mostly for processing the images.
- When both methods were used on the same day in 2023, the boat count found 11,840 nests and the drone count found 11,910.
